utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And we can see it says: "Subordinate the commanders of the newly established platoons ..." If we just stop there. What sort of platoons did you mean?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was precisely for that reason that I sought your clarification. What is implied here are the newly established platoons, and unless I'm mistaken, those were in Benkovac, Drnis, and now -- yes, correct. What is understood there is the military police platoon in Benkovac which had a reinforced squad in Obrovac, then the military police platoon in Drnis, then another one in the area of responsibility of the 71st Battalion in Gracac. Then a MP platoon in the Plitvice Lakes, then in the area of responsibility of the 730th Company, a MP company in Slunj. Within the 67th Battalion, a MP platoon in Glina, another one in Kostajnica, et cetera. What is implied here all these newly established platoons and the company, company in singular. The company, because it was the only newly established unit at the strength of a company in the newly liberated area. They were supposed to be subordinated to the most senior Croatian army commander in their areas of responsibility. In other words, the commanders of these platoons in Drnis, they were supposed to be subordinated to most senior commander in Drnis. The commander of the platoon in Benkovac was supposed to be subordinated to the most senior commander in Benkovac, et cetera; whereas, the commander of the military police company in Knin was supposed to be subordinated to the most senior commander in his area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm just allowing the translation to catch up as we have several languages here. I'm grateful for that. So looking at paragraph 14, we have in the English as plural, and I was going to ask you about that. It is it, in fact, in the singular. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's going confusing question without specifying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- what we should identify is whether there is an translation mistake, whether, if the original is in the plural, whether that is a mistake in drafting. We have to clearly make a distinction. First of all, in the original text is it in the plural? It is translated to us in the plural. How is it in your language? Company or companies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In singular, one company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is that how it -- and what word is that in the original? Could you pronounce it in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In daily operational command, commanders of the newly established platoons and the company of VP Knin are to be subordinated to the most senior ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just seeking, to the extent possible, from our interpreters, because it on the screen, whether it appears there as singular.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It does, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we have a translation mistake and nothing else. Could that be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is -- this is it a document that's already been put into evidence, and we will obviously get the record of the correct document into the court system. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lausic. Again, looking at the most senior Croatian commander, in the zone of responsibility, that is in fact not in accordance with Article 9, which says "by function." Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Article 9 uses the term "the most senior by position;" whereas, here, it says "the most senior command."

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. And in relation to that matter, the daily report of the Knin company should be sent to that person, is that correct, according to the system in paragraph 14?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, with the proviso that there was one peculiarity in Knin, and that was the following: In Knin a forward command post of the Military District of Split was located with the entire command. Knin was also the location of the forward command post of the 72nd Battalion of the military police together with its commander -- together with the commander of the 72nd Battalion. And militarily, it is quite understandable that the commander of one of the companies of the 72nd MP Battalion, which is located in Knin and whose area of responsibility that is, should not have communication with the command of the Military District. That is to say, the forward command post of the Military District because the command of the Military District receives reports from the 72nd Battalion of the military police, which cover all the activities performed by this company active in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just looking again at what was required in paragraph 14, the commander would be -- I'll read it out again. "In daily operational command subordinate the commanders of the newly established platoons and companies" -- "and company of the Knin military police." So just looking at that, in the terms of this order, your commander of the 72nd in Knin, Budimir, was required to do a positive act of subordinating the commander of the newly established company of the Knin military police to the most senior Croatian military commander by function in the zone of responsibility. Isn't that right? That required him to do a positive act to ensure subordination took place?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Based on this order that I issued, all battalion commanders, from whose battalions the newly established platoons and the company in Knin were formed, had to specify how this item 14 was to be implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Next matter, just looking at zone of responsibility. Was an order ever issued defining the zone of responsibility for the Knin company?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from the level of the military police administration. I don't know if the commander of the 72nd Battalion provided for that in his own order, but there was a binding instruction of the minister of defence -- we read a few days -- the minister of defence and chief of Main Staff at that time, General Bobetko, which specified exactly what is meant by the territory, the area of a certain Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Now, have you ever seen an order from Commander Budimir of the 72nd Military Police Battalion subordinating the Knin company to General Cermak, as required to put into effect your order at paragraph 14?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say either yes or no. It's possible that I have seen it. It's possible that I have not. I can't recall. If that order can be shown to me from which we could see that it was sent to the military police administration, and if the original that reached the military police administration could be provided, then we could see whether I signed it as received and whether it was forwarded to one of my officers who were in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, no. There is not a single document in the military police administration or from the 72nd Military Police Battalion from Commander Budimir making that subordination of the Knin company under General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. I mean, first of all, again, it's not precisely a question, although it can certainly be turned into a question. Secondly, it has a factual basis which may be a bit unclear to me, in any event how that determination was precisely made. I presume it means that none has been located during the course particular efforts. But I don't know what precisely those efforts are, exactly when they took place. But I think the question could be made somewhat clear in a number of ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, the witness said if you can show it to me and what you said, Mr. Kay. And I agree with Mr. Tieger to say that there does not exist a single document any -- what you could tell the witness that your Defence was not able to retrieve or has not received from any other source such a document so that you cannot show it to him. That's, I take it, what you wanted to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yeah. Well, it's not only me; it's the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is what I meant by other sources, which finally, of course, leaves open that -- but let's not make too much fuss about it. Mr. Kay cannot show it to you because is he not aware of the existence of such a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And who did how much -- it's best to find it is a matter we don't have to discuss at this moment. It's just not available in this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We will be looking at a number of other documents from the Knin company, and we will be able to comment on those, Mr. Lausic. There we are. That finishes that document then. I'd now like to turn to the Knin company. I have a photograph we can look at, 2D08-0047, and it's a photograph of the entrance to the Senjak barracks in Knin. First of all, have you been to the Senjak barracks where the forward command post of the 72nd Military Police Battalion was established in Knin?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I visited these barracks only in the late 1990s, 1998, if I'm not mistaken, or perhaps 1999. When the 72nd Battalion of the military police was moved to Split from [Realtime transcript read in error "from Split to Knin"]... Knin in its entirety, I was not here when the forward command post of the 72nd Battalion was located in these barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The translation I got was from Split to Knin in its entirety. Is that what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The translation and what we have on our transcript is, "when the 72nd Battalion of the military police was - there's a word missing - brought from Split to Knin in its entirety. Is that the right way around?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. In the years --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sorry. My mistake, and maybe I got confused, and I apologise. I can see now that that was right. Photograph here, which shows the entrance to the barracks, as you said, they were brought from Split to Knin to the barracks here. And was that a process that was set up in the days after the successful completion of Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm really sorry to interrupt, but now I'm -- I really am confused. I think the record is too. As I understood it, the original translation said "the 72nd was from Split to Knin." Mr. Kay started to correct that by saying "brought from Split to Knin," and accepted, as I understood it, that the original translation was correct. And now the "brought from Split to Knin" formulation is reintroduced when I thought it was accepted as being incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The "brought" was the missing word, and Split to Knin was the direction in which it apparently moved at a certain point in time. That's how I understood it. So, therefore, the think the correction was not about the "brought" but about what direction it went. But perhaps if you put your question in such a way that can be no confusion anymore, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And I apologise. I noticed the word missing the transcript here, and I was thrown off my stride. Perhaps I'm better off not reading the transcript at this distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it correct after the successful completion of Operation Storm that the 72nd brought their forward command post here to Knin?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forward command post of the 72nd Battalion was followed by the forward command post of the Military District of Split. When the forward command post of the 72nd Battalion was moved to Knin, I couldn't tell you, but it certainly followed the new location of the forward command post of the Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. And we will look at some more documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this photograph be made an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes exhibit number D1296.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1296 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. And the first document I would like to look at is 2D08-0025.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile I ask you, Mr. Kay, what exactly we would have to look at on the photograph? Or is it just --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It was a point of reference, that this was there, and there it is. And it may become more significant as a photograph further down the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll wait for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... process. Yes. If we could just go to the top of the English document, just so that we can see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 25th of July, 1995, and it's sent by Commander Budimir to you as a special report from Rujani. And Rujani was where the 72nd had their forward command post before it moved to Knin. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not answer this question precisely at this moment. At any rate, these activities were linked to the preparation for Operation Storm, but there is no mention here of the forward command post of the 72nd Battalion of the military police. The reference is instead to the forward command post of the joint company, which was an ad hoc unit within the 72nd Battalion made up of members of all organisational parts of the 72nd Battalion, and we can see that from the report itself. We can see all the elements that make up this joint company. So it's not about the forward command post of the 72nd Battalion, but the forward command post of that joint company of the 72nd Battalion. The forward command post of the 72nd Battalion was established only by my order that had been shown here earlier of the 3rd August, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And just for information purposes, we've got a document headed here "independent company," and I'm advised that the witness correctly translated it as "joint company" on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think that the witness translated anything, but what he said, what he read apparently was translated to us, again, as the joint company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you consider this to be the right translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. We will upload a fresh translation on this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then I take it that you will have that verified. Because if this is it rightly translated of what witness said, and, of course, there's one step in between this, whether he rightly read what is in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. We will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... deal with it. Nothing hangs on it at this stage, Your Honour. May this document be made an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1297, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1297 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The company being formed here, was that the preparation for the Knin company that was eventually formed?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not say. I could not answer this question. This joint company was formed to meet some needs that had arisen at that time in that area and to perform military police missions in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, apparently you're turning a page. If that would mean a new subject, then I'd like to have a break first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a break, and we will resume at ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Lausic, if we could just look at another document. It's 2D07-0005. It's from Commander Captain Dzolic of the joint company, operations group Sector North, dated 4th of August, 1995, to Major Juric, and it's a daily report for that day, and it's from Rujani, 4th of August. First of all, is this a document you've ever seen before?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The daily report for the 3rd to 4th of August sets out check-points that were established, and we have no need to look at the second page. It's just this. Where it's from, Rujani, was that the forward command post near Sajkovici of the 72nd Military Police Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you. I'm not familiar with these micro locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see what's said there. It's headed: "Joint company." Again, was this from the establishment we looked at earlier in the previous orders, which eventually became the Knin company, post-liberation of Knin; do you know?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer your question. What we have here are certainly the activities before the start of Operation Storm and the activities preceding the liberation of the town of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this become an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit D1298.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1298 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If we go to the next document, 2D08-0033.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's dated the 5th of August, 1995, from Commander Dzolic again. And comes from him at the 2nd Military Police Company of the 72nd Battalion and is a report on arrests. I just wondered if you were able to help with. This we see Commander Dzolic from the 2nd there, sending this report. But we have also seen him sending a report to Captain Juric, the previous exhibit, in relation to the joint company. Are you able to help us as to why that would be the case?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't be able to explain this. Unless I'm mistaken, Mr. Dzolic was a witness before this Tribunal, and he probably gave his explanation of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Lausic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1299, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1299 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Various orders and reports were made from the 5th of August concerning the Knin company, and if we can just look at only a few of those, of which there are several.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But if we could look at Exhibit P882.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which was a document issued by you on the 6th of August, 1995, to the Ministry of Defence and Chief of Staff. It ends 487. And it's your report on the use of military police units. And we can see in paragraph 1: "On the 4th and 5th of August, 1995, we undertook the following actions." And then you inform them about the establishment of the Knin company and the number of men and the fact that Captain Dzolic was performing the tasks in the town. Just looking at the detail there, would it be the case how the system worked that that information would have come up the chain to you from Major Juric, who was the superior officer of the 72nd at that time? Would he have briefed you about what was happening with the size of the company in Knin and its establishment?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my 2nd of August order, under item 12, it is stated that the commanders of the 72nd and 73rd Military Police Battalions would be reporting to Major Ivan Juric, the commander of the forward command post of the military police administration in the Split Military District, and he, in turn, would report to the MP administration every day by 2000 hours, starting from the 4th of August. Therefore, as far as the Split Military District is concerned, the reports reaching that quarter come from Major Ivan Juric.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, moving on in time a bit, is Exhibit P884, dated the 11th of August, 1995. It's not a document sent to you because it was a document concerning a meeting to be held in Knin at the military police building of the battalion command and the 72nd Military Police commanders of companies and platoons for a briefing. And we can see it was issued as an information by Commander Budimir and was an internal document. I'd just like to ask you system here. Presumably this was not a meeting that you or Mr. Biskic went to?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a document whereby the commander of the 72nd Battalion called a meeting of the command of the 72nd Battalion. The subordinate commanders of companies and platoons of the 72nd Military Police Battalion -- or, rather, summoning to a meeting the commanders of these various structures. Earlier on I said that the 72nd Battalion, had, as its area of responsibility, the area stretching from Pag to Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just one matter, and this is brought to my attention. Did you know that Brigadier Biskic did in fact attend this meeting in Knin on that day, and he was in Knin at that time?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, but I can't give you an answer at this time. As I said earlier on, in the course of Operation Storm and in the aftermath of the first several days of Operation Storm, I primarily toured the area of Kordun, Banja, and Lika, whereas my deputy covered the area of responsibility of the 72nd -- or, rather, of the 71st and 72nd Military Police Battalions. I can't, at this time, tell you exactly at which times he toured which parts of that territory. If he was present at this meeting, and if -- if notes were taken of the meeting, that document will show if my deputy, Brigadier Biskic, was present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Turning now to another document concerning the Knin company now. This is 2D07-0021. And it's dated the 14th of August, 1995. It's an order issued by you from the military police administration to the 66th and 72nd Military Police Battalions, concerning armoured vehicles to be used by the 72nd and to be transferred to them by the 66th. Just looking at the document there, Mr. Lausic, do you recognise this order?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I know the reasons underlying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That anticipates my next question, if you could assist the Court.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only combat armoured vehicles in the military police force were placed at the disposal of the 66th Military Police Battalion in Zagreb by virtue of the establishment. In the first days of Operation Storm, they were engaged in the areas of Banovina and Kordun. In order to increase the efficiency of the 72nd Military Police Battalion, and since the methods and tactics of action changed, as I said, the change concerned meant that they were supposed to start from the check-points out into the liberated areas for patrol beats. For this reason, this order was issued for the Knin MP company to be reinforced with two combat armoured vehicles from the 66th Battalion with crews in accordance with all the other items listed in the order. The aim was for the men of the company of the 72nd Battalion in Knin to become more efficient, more mobile, and more protected through the use of armoured vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this document become an Exhibit D, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1300, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1300 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Also of this date is the next document, and it follows on from what you've just been telling us. Can we see 2D07-0019. It's a document dated 14th of August, 1995. It's from the service for political activities of the 72nd VP, signed by the assistant commander, First Lieutenant Soldic, and it's a special report based on a warning that was issued and in which he says: "We are responsible for the newly liberated Croatian territory as a military police unit." First of all, is this a document that you have seen before?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't had the occasion to see the document. I don't know if you are familiar with the vertical subordination of officers for political activity in the HV units, as well as that of security officers in the HV.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, we've had evidence about that, that matter. Thank you very much. I'm looking at this document because he describes the military police tasks that, during Operation Storm and after it, he was carrying out. And you can see point 1, prevention of arson, et cetera; point 2, preventing killing of livestock; point 3, preventing war booty being wrongly extracted as well as theft of property; and preventing mistreatment of people. And as he ends: "On the top of the mentioned tasks which we carry out as priorities, we execute all other tasks in the newly liberated area of the Republic of Croatia that are part of the scope of work of the military police." First of all, are you able to help us with that last sentence that he wrote about concerning the tasks and the scope of the work of the military police?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we can see, he listed these four items as priorities. He also noted that all the other tasks from within the purview of the military police should be carried out, the ones which are listed in the rules on the organisation and work of the military police in Article 10, unless I'm mistaken. I don't know who the report was addressed to, but I suppose it was addressed to the assistant commander for political affairs, assistant commander to the Military District Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I ask about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May this be made an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1301, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We're now going to move to a different subject which concerns the appointment of the commander of the Knin military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So if we look at document Exhibit D789.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's dated the 17th of August, 1995. It's a order by Commander Budimir. And if you just look at that document, Mr. Lausic, and tell me -- if we can quickly go to page 2, we see that you're not part of the people that it's delivered to, but if we can just show you that page and then move back to page 1 so you've seen all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If we go back to page 1 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: First of all, is this a document that you've seen before?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is an order by Budimir in relation to the appointment of, as we see in paragraph 2, Lieutenant Orsulic as the joint company commander, various others as officers as well, and then the rotation in paragraph 3 of various officers from the 1st Company. Paragraph 4, the crime investigation department, duty service leader, logistic platoon commander select a rotation of officers. Paragraph 5, special attention should be paid that the best officers are selected because of specific tasks. Detailed military and psychological preparations. They shall be provided with necessary material, technical and quartermaster equipment. Where they are to assemble in Split, their transportation, and there's nothing material on the second page, other than the fact that the commanders mentioned in the order are responsible for its implementation. If we just look at the power that the order was made under, pursuant to the order of the chief of military police. And the power is given as being under the particular document 512-19-01-485, which is our document -- it's the 5th of August order, being exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We will tell everyone the magic number. Exhibit 881, P881. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And is regarding the needs arising in the newly liberated areas of the Republic of Croatia. Now, first of all, he cited that order of the 15th of August rather than the order of the 14th of August that we looked at an hour and a half ago. Is there any comment that you have on that, the fact that he didn't take the 14th of August order? Should he have taken that order as being the order by which he operated?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer your question specifically, although nothing changed in relation to the issue -- to the order issued by the commander of the 72nd Battalion. In addition to this 5 August order, I can only refer to the 14th of August order where, in item 12, it is specified that the newly formed MP units which certainly included the Knin MP Company, members of these units should be rotated every 20 days in such a way that 50 percent of the a given unit is rotated, in order to ensure continuity in the execution of military police tasks. I don't find anything disputable there, save for the fact that in the preamble the commander referred to my order of the 5th of August, but he did not also refer to the 14th of August order. We always have to be mindful of the fact that these were officers who did not graduate from Military Academies and committed former errors in drafting these orders. But this did not fundamentally detract anything from this particular order, the fact that it failed to refer to my 14th of August order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The order of 5th of August, 1995, ending 485, our Exhibit P881, was an order of a different nature, though. Would you like to remind yourself -- I see you've got your file there, and it might be prudent if you looked at it in the 5th of August to see it. That order was with a view to making preparations upon the successful completion of Operation Oluja. And in the terms of the order, there was a less detailed subordination under Article 7: "For the execution of daily operational command, the commanders of the newly established VP units shall be subordinated to the most senior HV commander in their respective zone of responsibility." Moving to the other exhibit, D47, of the 14th of August, ending in 530. And we've looked there at paragraph 14 of the nature of the order that says normalize the command and control structure. And we looked at the issue of subordination earlier this morning. Turning back then to Exhibit D789. As a matter of form, should Commander Budimir have been exercising his authority under the later order of the 14th of August or this one of the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only repeat the answer I've given already; namely, that what we see in the preamble of this order, in addition to the reference to my order of the 5th of August, there is no reference to the order of the 14th of August, does not change anything substantially, because in the order of the commander of the 72nd Battalion, there is it only mention of the rotation of forces of the newly established company in Knin, together with all the details we read in this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It contains the detail of the rotation, but also in paragraph 2, it is also the appointment of First Lieutenant Orsulic, as the joint company commander. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It's also rotation of commanders. If I'm not mistaken, the first commander was the commander of the 1st Battalion, Captain Bojnic, and he is now replaced by Captain Orsulic, and the rest of the unit is also replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I just follow what you've said there as it is not clear to me. We can see in 2 that Orsulic is appointed, but you said the first commander was the commander of the 1st Battalion, Captain Bojnic, who is now replaced by Captain Orsulic. Did you mean Captain Dzolic whose orders we looked at earlier this morning?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the first commander of the joint company of the military police of the 72nd Battalion - that is to say, the newly established MP company - was Captain Bosko Dzolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think we may have had an interpretation wrong there of the name, Your Honour, which is why I asked the question about Bojnic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This being clarified, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Now, this document as an appointment of Lieutenant Orsulic and the rest of the officers, if we turn to page 2, was delivered to the commander, and the commander is Lieutenant Orsulic. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not give you a precise answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The other companies of the battalions of the 72nd that we see set out, but it is not sent to the Knin garrison, Knin ZM. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only confirm what I see in the document; namely, to whom it was addressed, to whom this order was delivered. I can neither confirm nor deny what you're asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And when I asked you earlier today about any document showing the positive act of subordination by Commander Budimir under General Cermak, would you agree that if that had happened, General Cermak would have been copied in on this information by Commander Budimir so that it was known to whom Lieutenant Orsulic reported and to whom he was subordinated?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, as I replied earlier to Mr. Misetic that I am reluctant to answer hypothetical questions, I would say the same here. I can't say what have happened if it had been. We have an order to rotate the MP company in Knin from the Force Commander, we see to whom it was sent, and I can only give my opinion based on those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Wouldn't information like this be essential to be passed from one area, namely, the commander of the military police, to the garrison commander if he was subordinating Lieutenant Orsulic, commander of the Knin company, to another officer?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer to your question I could give only if I had specific knowledge that the commander of the 72nd Battalion had not informed the commander of the Military District in any form.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: That is, the commander of the garrison. Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this moment, I don't know whether the garrison commander was aware of this. That is, the new chain of command for the military police in Knin or whether he was informed only when the new commander reported to him to receive orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could turn now to another document, Exhibit D791. This is a document from the 21st of August, 1995, from Commander Orsulic. He sent it to the general military police section of the military police administration. It concerns a security report, how, between 1030 and 1900 on the 19th of August, a working group from the Ministry of Defence were secured during a tour of military facilities, and on the 20th of August, similar information. Would it not have been the case if -- first of all, have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. However, there's nothing disputable about this document. Nothing controversial.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. What I'd like to ask you is this: If General Cermak was in command of the military police, wouldn't this report have been sent to him to inform him of a regular task that the Knin company had carried out on these days?

utterances.speaker: MATE LAUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is precisely, Mr. Kay, one of the extraordinary tasks that follow within the purview of the military police. As far as I can see from the document itself, the military police administration, its department of general military police, the section for security and anti-explosive security - that is, the bomb squad - sent this order about securing a working group from the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia that was touring and inspecting military installations in the area. The extraordinary task consisted in providing military police security for that working group, stationary and moving, and this is a report that this task had been accomplished. There's one illogical aspect, namely, why this was sent to this section directly from the company commander, rather than sent to the administration from the 72nd Battalion commander, but such irregularities did happen on the part of commanders in those years. But I repeat, this was a task clearly within the purview of the military police. It was carried out, and its completion was notified to the level that had issued the order. Whether this task was covered in the daily report for 19 August, the report of the MP company Knin, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We will look at the daily reports tomorrow as I notice the hour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I appreciate it. Many of those who are assisting counsel are assisting me as well in the task of drawing the attention to the clock or to the speed of speech. Mr. Lausic, same instructions as I gave you before; that is, not to speak with anyone about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow, 9.00, in this same courtroom. We adjourn and resume on Tuesday, 3rd of February, 9.00, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 3rd day of February, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
